comments.text:
It's the QUALITY of food that sucks! And add the crappy chemicals in the food, which you will never see in other countries. I mean, think about it: Starbucks gives us options to top them 15-25%! Why exactly?

I have been to 47 countries to date; the worst food quality and the most overpriced ones are in our country. You eat fish, meat, veggies, or chicken in Spain, Croatia, Morocco, China, India, Korea, Japan, Singapore, France, Italy, Greece, or Serbia... and then compare the same in the USA, you will know what I am talking about. And the prices, when you compare the quality, are often 3-4 times higher in the USA. 

And then comes the tipping! I am sick and tired of it, and I am sure many are. Yes, you can argue your hearts out; that's our culture. No, it's not! It was created by the business owners who refuse to pay better wages and are sucking up our wages, and we are supporting this wrong cause. 

And now the worst part: adding a 20% surcharge on the bill for bringing 4 people to eat - what?? So if you bring your family of four to dinner/ lunch, you HAVE TO PAY 20% extra, and this is not the tip! So why would anyone go there? I have stopped! 

So here's my take: I would rather make my own meal and breakfast, which is a hundred times better in quality and saves me hundreds of dollars per month. I only go to restaurants abroad for peace of mind with quality and price, and not paying insane surcharges. They can eat their own food!

Give me a break in case you forgot here's the 7:26 A restaurant menu price typically breaks down into four main categories:

​Raw Ingredients (COGS): ~30%

​Labor & Payroll: ~30%

​Overhead (Rent, Utilities, Insurance, Software): ~25–30%

​Profit Margin: ~3–10%

​What Restaurants Pay vs. What Customers Pay

Restaurants pay for every operational cost behind the scenes—from wholesale food, spoilage, and staff hourly wages to credit card processing fees, rent, and utility bills. Customers pay a single marked-up price that covers these combined expenses plus a small profit margin.

​How They Calculate Menu Prices

Most restaurants use a target food cost percentage (usually around 30%).

comments.text: Went to a local vegan place that has stellar reviews, was curious how they made a vegan breakfast burrito. Got the (rather small) burrito and a small coffee. Like the reviews said, the food was great! However it was $30 for those two items, and that's why I won't return.

replies.author: @OrthoDuck
replies.text: Another thing is a lot of these businesses are renting their retail space and rents have doubled in the last 6 years.

replies.author: @OrthoDuck
replies.text: Oh yeah and when I was young, tipping was 10% for bad, 15% standard, 20% good, now its 20% bad, 25% standard, 30% good. I've also seen retail businesses ask for tips when I buy stuff online.

comments.author: @jodifrangello4574
comments.text:
People are tired of being served substandard foods, along with the fact that servers are Not trained properly! Substandard food and substandard service leads to lower tips and less revenue for the establishment! Managers and owners need to start, insisting on properly trained, seasoned staff! If your chefs And line cooks will not follow your instructions and Recipes, Management needs to get in the kitchen until such time they find a cook or chef willing to follow the recipes! 
Speaking from experience  😏
Also, as a consumer, we no longer patronize several restaurants we patronized for decades, due to poor quality of staff!
Prices go up, quality of food goes down, and service is sub standard  🤷‍♀️ What would you expect would happen?
As for Prices rocketing to the absurd, you have all the bleeding heart liberal politicians to blame for that! I was a server for over 20 years, I would never work for $16 an hour! Any server worth their weight and salt can earn anywhere between 25 and $40 an hour in tips! I sometimes got yelled at from the office for not picking up checks for over a month 🧐😂 The nonsense about minimum wage is another reason you have poorly trained servers!
